initial_source_observation.meaning: The measurement carries elapsed real time. The spectrum carries live time and references identifying its detector and energy calibration. Preserve these subjects when testing overlap.

exchange.finding: The document gathers descriptions, measurements, calibrations and analytical results under a radiation instrument output. Resource IDs for references are document-scoped. Optional and required ID bases and the document UUID have different purposes.
exchange.comparison_test: Keep an exchange identifier distinct from a physical serial number or persistent web identity.

equipment.finding: An instrument has manufacturer, identifier, model, class and component versions. Its detector descriptions have radiation category, physical detector kind, description and size or volume. A quality-control entry pairs inspection time with calibration standing.
equipment.comparison_test: Which device, which detector, and when was calibration standing inspected?

item.finding: The inspected item has its own description, measurement geometry, characteristics and optional amount with units and uncertainty.
item.comparison_test: Keep identity, geometry and location of the inspected subject separate from those of the detector.

characteristics.finding: Additional characteristics can be grouped. A characteristic carries its name, value, unit and data class with optional value time and out-of-limits indication.
characteristics.comparison_test: Store a typed, unit-qualified value and the subject to which it applies.

state.finding: Instrument, detector and item states reference their respective descriptions. A measurement can carry all three. Instrument state may contain mode, faults and movement. Detector fault or state must be attributed to that detector.
state.comparison_test: Separate technical state from observations and qualify faults by affected equipment.

location.finding: Position, orientation and speed may describe instrument, detector or inspected item. A position may use a geographic point, description or relative representation with origin. Geographic-point accuracy, elevation offset and datum have distinct subjects.
location.comparison_test: Show whose position and which origin/axis apply; avoid treating shielding or a source estimate as instrument placement.

acquisition.finding: A common acquisition period has a class, start and real duration. It may refer to inspected items and more than one measurement group. Occupancy refers to the measured item during that interval.
acquisition.comparison_test: Distinguish foreground, background, calibration and intrinsic activity; use occupancy only for its stated field of view and acquisition.

spectrum.finding: A spectrum has counts by channel, detector live duration and an energy calibration reference. Different compression choices can represent the same channel sequence. Detector live duration describes sensitivity during acquisition and may be shorter than elapsed time.
spectrum.comparison_test: Preserve raw counts, channel indexing, detector association and calibrations before showing calibrated spectrum or comparison.

calibration.finding: A channel-energy mapping can use coefficients or bin boundaries. Energy/deviation pairs can correct the mapping. Resolution and efficiency curves are separately keyed to energies, may carry uncertainty, and are distinct from the calibration date. Energy windows pair limits.
calibration.comparison_test: Keep a curve’s purpose and ordered values. Distinguish single/double escape and full-energy efficiencies, resolution, and total efficiency.

count_dose_exposure.finding: Counts acquired over a live interval differ from totals since reset. Energy windows may partition counts. Dose-rate fields use microsieverts per hour, and exposure-rate fields use milliroentgens per hour. The corresponding totals have different units from their rates.
count_dose_exposure.comparison_test: Preserve quantity kind, units, duration, accumulation basis, detector and window scope; do not infer dose from an uncalibrated count.

derived.finding: Derived measurement-like data have an analysis origin. Result objects may reference raw objects of the corresponding kind. The input links and origin provide information beyond the form of the numeric output.
derived.comparison_test: Identify derivation and raw contributors separately from instrument and detector IDs.

analysis.finding: An analysis can refer separately to measurements, measurement groups and derived data. The result can carry algorithm identity, settings, version, processing time, state, confidence, faults and specific result families.
analysis.comparison_test: Show which inputs an analysis consumed and identify its algorithm/configuration at the time.

nuclide_peaks.finding: The nuclide identification indicator, confidence representations, activity estimate, uncertainty and minimum detectable activity answer different questions. Geometry, shielding and position qualify the source. Peak evidence can identify expected/measured energy, peak width, net area and uncertainty.
nuclide_peaks.comparison_test: Separate a nuclide identification claim from peak evidence, an uncertain activity estimate and a sensitivity limit.

result_statistics.finding: Analysis summaries carry quantity-specific averages, uncertainties, minima, maxima, background estimates, totals and possible source position.
result_statistics.comparison_test: Keep background distinct from an ordinary minimum and qualify all statistics by the result family.

alarms.finding: An alarm references affected detectors and can identify triggering window indices and reported audible or visual indication. An equipment Fault has different semantics.
alarms.comparison_test: Retain alarm subject and condition; a measurement group or analytical alarm does not imply a device fault.

media.finding: Embedded content or a file reference can describe an inspected item. Capture duration, device identity, sequence, perspective, media kind and image dimensions are independently meaningful.
media.comparison_test: Associate media with the inspected items and capture device without assigning everything to the main radiation detector.

encoding.finding: Numeric and list types constrain lexical representation, ranges and fixed units. The same scalar or list can serve different semantic roles through its owning field.
encoding.comparison_test: Carry units, type and range through interpretation; primitive types in isolation provide no equipment concept.

extensions.finding: The main schema supplies extension substitution points. The illustrative add-in qualifies its fields in a different namespace.
extensions.comparison_test: Keep the extension definition, owner and applicability with the field; do not give an example the standing of a required base field.

schema_contact.edition_note: Edition selected by publisher page and pinned file hash. The 2011 target namespace is shared across these 2020-package examples.
schema_contact.accounting: Global declaration membership is exhaustive in the pinned XSD. Group summaries synthesize related subjects; they do not imply each declaration is a new row. The original XSD defines all local names, types, occurrences, choices and references. Marked local constraints were checked for claims that depend on cardinality.
schema_contact.extension: Both add-in declarations are illustrative RadMeasurementExtension substitutions. XSD validation bound the add-in author-local import URI to the fingerprinted main schema in memory.

schematron.execution: Compiled the original NIST ISO Schematron using SchXslt 1.10.1 pipeline-for-svrl.xsl with SaxonC-HE 13.1. Evaluated its XPath against all 11 XSD-validated examples. For ID-dependent evaluation, an in-memory-equivalent working copy used an internal DTD declaring each existing id as XML ID for the elements carrying it. Instance elements, attributes and values were preserved. Ordinary untyped Saxon input discards XSD ID typing and produces spurious id() failures. All 11 ID-aware examples returned zero failed assertions. This validates examples against the tested files only.

examples.xsd: valid with add-in and pinned primary schema

S06-R001.label: Manufacturer name
S06-R001.reason: Names the manufacturer of the radiation measurement instrument that collected the data.

S06-R002.label: Product model designation
S06-R002.reason: Reports the instrument product model separately from its individual identifier.

S06-R003.label: Individual hardware serial number
S06-R003.reason: An instrument identifier may contain a serial number or an asset tag. A value should be labeled serial only when its authority or context supports that interpretation.

S06-R004.label: Persistent System identifier
S06-R004.reason: The instrument identifier concerns the physical unit; the XML ID and document UUID have different scopes. No persistence policy for a general system identifier is established.

ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST.label: Certificate identity and trust context
ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST.reason: The document identifies equipment and its results. It defines no certificate issuer, trust chain or permitted credential use for a network connection.

S06-R005.label: Described sensing System / arrangement
S06-R005.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadInstrumentInformation; RadInstrumentClassCodeSimpleType/Network Area Monitor
S06-R005.reason: RadInstrumentInformation describes the instrument that collected the data. The Network Area Monitor class explicitly includes several radiation instruments working as one, supporting an arrangement as the described subject.

S06-R006.label: Network-visible participant
S06-R006.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
S06-R006.reason: An instrument represented in an exchange document need not be an addressable participant on a network.

SAPIENT-F2-FUSION-ROLE.label: Candidate — Hierarchical fusion Node role and aggregated capabilities
SAPIENT-F2-FUSION-ROLE.reason: Network Area Monitor explicitly treats several instruments as a single instrument. It supplies neither a fusion-node role nor a hierarchy of capability advertisements.

S06-R007.label: Physical constituent
S06-R007.locator: N42 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType/RadDetectorInformation; Annex B instrument and detector
S06-R007.reason: The file identifies detectors of the described instrument. Its document structure alone does not establish a mechanical subassembly, nesting depth or containment hierarchy.

S06-R008.label: Connected external equipment
S06-R008.reason: The document can describe multiple detectors. It does not declare the external cabling or connection topology of separately managed equipment.

S06-R009.label: Hosting platform / station context
S06-R009.reason: A state vector can locate either the instrument or a detector. It does not identify an independently described host platform or station.

S06-R010.label: Observing procedure / method
S06-R010.reason: Names and versions of the algorithm that processed radiation data concern analysis. They do not identify an acquisition procedure for every observation.

ISA-A-PARTICIPATION.label: Network participation role and responsibilities
ISA-A-PARTICIPATION.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-A-PARTICIPATION.reason: The exchange schema describes collected data. It supplies no network connection or management-path contract for network participation role and responsibilities.

ISA-A-NETWORK-CONTEXT.label: Network instance and connection context
ISA-A-NETWORK-CONTEXT.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-A-NETWORK-CONTEXT.reason: The exchange schema describes collected data. It supplies no network connection or management-path contract for network instance and connection context.

SOSA-F2-MGMT-PATH.label: Candidate — delegated and independent hardware-management path
SOSA-F2-MGMT-PATH.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
SOSA-F2-MGMT-PATH.reason: The exchange schema describes collected data. It supplies no network connection or management-path contract for delegated and independent hardware-management path.

ISA-A-MEMBER-EXPOSURE.label: Composition member exposure and source attribution
ISA-A-MEMBER-EXPOSURE.reason: A measurement can refer to the detector that collected it. Document-level attribution supplies no capability-publication or member-visibility policy for a composition interface.

ISA-A-PARTICIPATION-LIFECYCLE.label: Connection-specific network participation lifecycle
ISA-A-PARTICIPATION-LIFECYCLE.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-A-PARTICIPATION-LIFECYCLE.reason: The exchange schema describes collected data. It supplies no network connection or management-path contract for connection-specific network participation lifecycle.

S06-R011.label: Addressed transducer channel
S06-R011.reason: In this spectrum an energy channel is a bin in a sequence of counts. The spectrum can point to detector information; the bin has no independent transducer address.

S06-R012.label: Reported output field
S06-R012.reason: The measurement can carry distinctly typed reported fields for counts, dose rate or spectral channels. Instrument and detector state have their own elements.

S06-R013.label: Observed / observable property
S06-R013.reason: Named radiation quantities distinguish the meaning of reported values. Other observed properties and an independent observed-property catalog need their own definitions.

S06-R014.label: Observer / observing System
S06-R014.reason: Instrument information identifies the collecting instrument. The XSD allows the detector reference on a spectrum to be omitted; the Schematron separately checks same-detector spectrum siblings within a measurement. Creator identity applies to the file.

S06-R015.label: Performed Observation
S06-R015.reason: A measurement record describes a collection with a start, elapsed duration and acquisition class. A publisher example illustrates the record format only.

SAPIENT-F2-TARGET-CLAIMS.label: Candidate — Detected target taxonomy, behavior and confidence assertions
SAPIENT-F2-TARGET-CLAIMS.reason: Nuclide name, identification status and algorithm-dependent certainty refer to a radiation analysis. They do not classify the behavior or target hypothesis of a SAPIENT detection.

ISA-C-123.label: Observed atmospheric cloud-layer descriptions
ISA-C-123.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric cloud-layer descriptions.

ISA-C-124.label: Observed atmospheric dew-point temperature
ISA-C-124.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric dew-point temperature.

ISA-C-125.label: Observed atmospheric relative humidity
ISA-C-125.locator: NIST N42SchemaAddin-2020.xsd, HumidityValue; Annex L example
ISA-C-125.reason: The example add-in defines relative humidity at measurement time and place. This is a vendor-namespace extension illustrating a way to carry environmental context.

ISA-C-126.label: Observed atmospheric precipitation category and rate
ISA-C-126.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric precipitation category and rate.

ISA-C-127.label: Observed atmospheric pressure
ISA-C-127.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric pressure.

ISA-C-128.label: Observed atmospheric temperature
ISA-C-128.locator: NIST N42SchemaAddin-2020.xsd, TemperatureValue; Annex L example
ISA-C-128.reason: The example add-in defines ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at measurement time and place. An instance using only the core schema has no such dedicated field.

ISA-C-129.label: Observed atmospheric visibility condition and distance
ISA-C-129.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric visibility condition and distance.

ISA-C-130.label: Observed atmospheric wind category, speed and direction
ISA-C-130.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed atmospheric wind category, speed and direction.

ISA-C-122.label: Observation-associated geographic shape
ISA-C-122.reason: A source position may be a point, relative location or textual location. This supplies no general polygon or area geometry.

ISA-C-133.label: Observed-entity bearing relative to observer orientation
ISA-C-133.reason: RelativeLocationAzimuthValue provides a bearing from a reference point. Confirm that the Origin identifies the observer and check its directional convention before comparing the ISA bearing.

ISA-C-141.label: Reported observer-to-entity distance
ISA-C-141.reason: Distance can be given relative to a stated origin. The origin must identify the observer before interpreting this as observer-to-item range.

ISA-C-149.label: Reported entity impact position
ISA-C-149.reason: Source and measured-item positions have no encoded role as a point of impact.

ISA-C-150.label: Reported entity launch position
ISA-C-150.reason: Source and measured-item positions have no encoded role as a point of launch.

ISA-C-151.label: Observed-entity position at observation
ISA-C-151.reason: A measured item can carry a state vector in a particular measurement with absolute or relative location.

ISA-C-159.label: Observed-entity velocity at observation
ISA-C-159.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadItemStateType/StateVector; SpeedValue documentation, OrientationType
ISA-C-159.reason: SpeedValue is scalar. Its definition explicitly assigns direction along the orientation bearing when Orientation is present. Without that bearing the item speed alone gives no velocity direction.

ISA-C-131.label: Observed-entity battle-space identifier
ISA-C-131.locator: N42 2020 XSD, RadItemInformationType and document-scoped references
ISA-C-131.reason: Measured-item references identify records within the document. They do not assert a battle-space identifier.

ISA-C-140.label: Human-readable observation comment
ISA-C-140.locator: N42 2020 XSD, Remark, ReqIdComplexObjectType/Remark and RadMeasurementType
ISA-C-140.reason: The common object base allows a human-readable comment attached to a specific measurement.

ISA-C-142.label: Explanation for OTHER event type
ISA-C-142.reason: Free text can explain a record or alarm. No field specifically requires an explanation conditioned on an OTHER event type.

ISA-C-145.label: Reported tactical identity of observed entity
ISA-C-145.reason: A measured item and identified nuclide do not express the tactical affiliation of an observed entity.

ISA-C-146.label: Media resources associated with observation
ISA-C-146.reason: The exchange can include linked or embedded media and associate it with measured items. Item association alone does not link the media to a particular observation event.

ISA-C-147.label: Reported primary event-generation method
ISA-C-147.reason: The algorithm can be attributed to the analysis that produced results or alarms. A general event-generation method vocabulary is not defined.

ISA-C-160.label: Attributed verifier of event contents
ISA-C-160.reason: The organization that created the document and the algorithm creator have defined roles. Neither field designates a verifier of a reported event.

ISA-C-134.label: Reported biological contour-level map
ISA-C-134.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined reported biological contour-level map field.

ISA-C-135.label: Detailed reported biological analysis levels
ISA-C-135.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined detailed reported biological analysis levels field.

ISA-C-136.label: Reported biological sample-analysis reading
ISA-C-136.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined reported biological sample-analysis reading field.

ISA-C-137.label: Reported chemical contour-level map
ISA-C-137.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined reported chemical contour-level map field.

ISA-C-138.label: Detailed reported chemical analysis levels
ISA-C-138.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined detailed reported chemical analysis levels field.

ISA-C-139.label: Reported chemical sample-analysis reading
ISA-C-139.reason: Radiation counts, doses, spectra and nuclide analysis supply no defined reported chemical sample-analysis reading field.

ISA-C-144.label: Reported hazard areas associated with an event
ISA-C-144.reason: An alarm can refer to a detector and an analysis can locate a source. These definitions do not delineate a geographic hazard area.

ISA-C-148.label: Reported nuclear-event descriptive information
ISA-C-148.reason: Radiation measurements and nuclide identifications might inform a nuclear-event report. The format does not itself assert a nuclear event or describe its phenomenology.

ISA-C-153.label: Reported radiation contour map
ISA-C-153.reason: Individual source positions, dose estimates and extrema do not form a radiation contour map.

ISA-C-154.label: Reported detailed radiation analysis levels
ISA-C-154.reason: Nuclide identity, category and identification confidence overlap the classified result in ISA-OBS-154. N42 also distinguishes count statistics and dose estimates. ISA’s arbitrary levels and readings cannot be assigned the same units by inference.

ISA-C-155.label: Reported radiation reading
ISA-C-155.locator: N42 2020 XSD, RadMeasurementType/DoseRate, TotalDose; NuclideType/NuclideName, NuclideActivityValue; ISA-OBS-155
ISA-C-155.reason: Identified nuclide and activity overlap. N42 dose fields measure ambient dose equivalent in microsieverts or microsieverts per hour. ISA also allows absorbed dose in gray; these are different quantities.

ISA-C-132.label: Inferred past observation statements
ISA-C-132.reason: Computed products can cite earlier measurements. Processing those measurements does not by itself establish a backcast about a past state.

ISA-C-143.label: Forecast observation statements
ISA-C-143.reason: Defined derived and analytical results describe collected radiation data. They do not represent a forecast time and predicted observation.

ISA-C-152.label: Processed video-frame report
ISA-C-152.reason: Media dimensions, perspective and capture time are represented; a video-frame processing result and frame-analysis fields are not established.

ISA-C-156.label: Referenced-event recall reason
ISA-C-156.reason: Alarm description and analysis status do not encode withdrawal of an earlier event and a reason.

ISA-C-157.label: Referenced-event resolution reason
ISA-C-157.reason: Alarm description and analysis status do not encode resolution of an earlier event and a reason.

ISA-C-158.label: Observed solar irradiance
ISA-C-158.reason: The core radiation result types and the published two-element environmental extension define no value for observed solar irradiance.

ISA-T-EVENT-ID.label: Source-qualified event identity and reference
ISA-T-EVENT-ID.reason: Alarm identity, event time and detector references are distinguishable. An optional document-local ID does not guarantee an event key scoped by a creating network participant.

ISA-T-EVENT-TIME.label: Event occurrence time
ISA-T-EVENT-TIME.reason: An issued radiation alarm can carry the date and time of the alarm.

ISA-T-EVENT-REASON.label: Event creation category
ISA-T-EVENT-REASON.reason: The category classifies an issued radiation alarm; the measurement class identifies a kind of acquisition. Neither field states a generic reason for creating an exchange event.

ISA-T-EVENT-CONTEXT.label: Detector property context at event occurrence
ISA-T-EVENT-CONTEXT.reason: A measurement may carry characteristics and state for the referenced detector at acquisition. This does not imply that the values differ from the last status message.

ISA-R-MEASUREMENT.label: Reported value and associated uncertainty
ISA-R-MEASUREMENT.reason: Values and their uncertainties are separately defined for particular radiation quantities. Each uncertainty must retain its subject and stated units.

ISA-R-VIDEO-DETECTION.label: Video-frame detection details
ISA-R-VIDEO-DETECTION.reason: Media metadata and nuclide identification confidence do not define a video-frame bounding rectangle or track association.

ISA-R-VIDEO-TRACK.label: Video-derived entity track reference
ISA-R-VIDEO-TRACK.reason: A link from media to measured items is not a video-derived track identifier.

ISA-K-CAPABILITIES.label: Declared component capability catalogue
ISA-K-CAPABILITIES.reason: The schema records instrument and detector descriptions and characteristics. No manifest of supported properties, commands and custom structures is defined.

SAPIENT-F2-PERFORMANCE.label: Candidate — Declared detection performance and geometric error
SAPIENT-F2-PERFORMANCE.reason: Accuracy for a particular point and a minimum detectable activity in a nuclide analysis are context-specific evidence. They do not declare the instrument’s registered detection performance envelope.

ISA-K-PROPERTY-DECL.label: Declared property definition
ISA-K-PROPERTY-DECL.reason: A reported characteristic can carry name, value, units and data class. The format does not require an independent device declaration with validity and publication rules.

ISA-K-OBSERVABLE-DECL.label: Declared observable definition
ISA-K-OBSERVABLE-DECL.reason: A schema names allowed radiation results and a detector category. An instance does not thereby advertise every observable the device supports.

ISA-K-COMMAND-DECL.label: Declared command interface
ISA-K-COMMAND-DECL.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-K-COMMAND-DECL.reason: The file format supplies no instrument control contract for declared command interface.

ISA-K-PARAMETER-DECL.label: Declared command parameter
ISA-K-PARAMETER-DECL.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-K-PARAMETER-DECL.reason: The file format supplies no instrument control contract for declared command parameter.

ISA-K-RESULT-DECL.label: Declared command result
ISA-K-RESULT-DECL.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-K-RESULT-DECL.reason: The file format supplies no instrument control contract for declared command result.

ISA-K-CUSTOM-TYPE.label: Declared custom data structure
ISA-K-CUSTOM-TYPE.locator: NIST add-in XSD, HumidityValue and TemperatureValue substitutions for RadMeasurementExtension; primary XSD extension elements
ISA-K-CUSTOM-TYPE.reason: An external schema can declare elements substituting for an extension point. The NIST add-in declares two simple elements; it does not demonstrate a component reporting a named custom structure and its field catalogue.

ISA-K-FIELD-DECL.label: Declared field within a custom structure
ISA-K-FIELD-DECL.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadMeasurementExtension substitution group; illustrative N42SchemaAddin-2020.xsd/HumidityValue, TemperatureValue
ISA-K-FIELD-DECL.reason: An externally declared extension element has a name and a type. These schema-level field definitions provide part of a custom field contract. Instance-specific capability declarations and omission rules for a device-defined structure are separate.

ISA-K-TYPE-CHOICE.label: Declared built-in or custom value type
ISA-K-TYPE-CHOICE.locator: N42 2020 XSD, CharacteristicValueDataClassCode, ChannelDataType; add-in XSD TemperatureValue/@type
ISA-K-TYPE-CHOICE.reason: Schema-defined types coexist with XML built-in types. A reported characteristic can identify its value class, without a device negotiating or declaring a new type.

ISA-K-STRUCTURE.label: Declared value shape and collection bounds
ISA-K-STRUCTURE.reason: The XSD constrains repetitions of document elements and declares a list type for channel data. These rules govern documents; an equipment declaration of the permitted shape and bounds for its own property has no established counterpart.

ISA-K-VALUE-RANGE.label: Declared permitted or excluded values
ISA-K-VALUE-RANGE.locator: N42 2020 XSD, Angle90Type, Angle180Type and associated simple types
ISA-K-VALUE-RANGE.reason: N42 defines restricted types and code lists in its publication. An instance reporting a characteristic does not thereby publish the device-specific allowed and excluded values of that property.

ISA-K-MUTABILITY.label: Declared property mutability
ISA-K-MUTABILITY.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType
ISA-K-MUTABILITY.reason: The file format supplies no instrument control contract for declared property mutability.

ISA-K-ABS-THRESHOLD.label: Absolute-value publication threshold
ISA-K-ABS-THRESHOLD.reason: An issued alarm or out-of-limits flag is evidence about a result. It does not define absolute-value publication threshold for property publication.

ISA-K-REL-THRESHOLD.label: Relative-change publication threshold and reference basis
ISA-K-REL-THRESHOLD.reason: An issued alarm or out-of-limits flag is evidence about a result. It does not define relative-change publication threshold and reference basis for property publication.

ISA-K-THRESHOLDS.label: Declared property publication triggers
ISA-K-THRESHOLDS.reason: An issued alarm or out-of-limits flag is evidence about a result. It does not define declared property publication triggers for property publication.

S06-R016.label: Supported operating mode
S06-R016.reason: The state record can name the operating mode of the instrument when measured. This does not enumerate its supported modes.

S06-R017.label: Declared default mode
S06-R017.reason: The state record describes the reported mode. It supplies no default mode declaration.

S06-R018.label: Source-reported operating mode
S06-R018.reason: The measured instrument can report its operating mode with its state during acquisition.

S06-R019.label: Issued control request
S06-R019.locator: NIST N42.42 project, Description; 2020 XSD, RadInstrumentDataType

N4242-LIVE.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RealTimeDuration, LiveTimeDuration, SpectrumType and GrossCountsType

N4242-CHANNELS.label: Detector-specific spectral counts by channel

N4242-ENERGY.label: Channel-to-energy mapping and energy calibration corrections

N4242-RESOLUTION.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, FWHMCalibrationType; SpectrumType/@FWHMCalibrationReference; Schematron EnergyFWHMMatch; Annex C

N4242-EFFICIENCY.label: Energy-dependent detector efficiency and its reference basis

N4242-ITEM.definition: Identify the measured item and any amount, associated units and one-sigma uncertainty. Preserve the description of the item shape, placement, orientation and attenuators used for this acquisition.
N4242-ITEM.reason: A geographic shape or instrument mounting position cannot recover how the item was presented to the detector or how much item material was measured.
N4242-ITEM.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, RadItemInformationType/RadItemQuantity and RadItemMeasurementGeometryDescription; RadMeasurementType/@radItemInformationReferences

N4242-LIVE.label: Elapsed acquisition duration and detector live duration
N4242-LIVE.definition: Preserve positive elapsed clock duration for the measurement and nonnegative sensitive duration for the contributing detection assembly. Detector live time excludes event-processing dead time and cannot exceed elapsed real time. Associate each duration with its spectrum or gross counts and the correct measurement.
N4242-LIVE.reason: Report times, uptime and averaging windows cannot show how long a particular detector could register counts during the measurement.
N4242-LIVE.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, RadMeasurementType/RealTimeDuration; SpectrumType/LiveTimeDuration; GrossCountsType/LiveTimeDuration; Annex B

N4242-CHANNELS.label: Detector-specific spectral counts by channel
N4242-CHANNELS.definition: Retain channel order, the represented counts and the spectrum’s energy-calibration reference. Keep the contributing detector reference when supplied. Missing compressionCode means uncompressed. Under CountedZeroes, a zero and the following number together encode that many zero-valued channels.
N4242-CHANNELS.reason: A reported field or digitized waveform has no intrinsic radiation channel ordering, zero-run convention or per-detector spectrum attribution.
N4242-CHANNELS.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, SpectrumType/@radDetectorInformationReference and ChannelData; ChannelDataType/@compressionCode; Annex B

N4242-ENERGY.label: Channel-to-energy mapping and energy calibration corrections
N4242-ENERGY.definition: Associate each spectrum with its energy calibration. Coefficient representation uses three ordered terms (offset, gain, quadratic), with zero quadratic term for a linear calibration. Boundary representation supplies an increasing list of channel-start energies plus the final upper edge. Apply any paired predicted-energy/deviation correction to the coefficient result.
N4242-ENERGY.reason: A set of calibration points does not say how to assign the energy bounds of an individual spectrum channel or apply a correction to the predicted energy.
N4242-ENERGY.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, EnergyCalibrationType; CoefficientValues, EnergyBoundaryValues, EnergyValues, EnergyDeviationValues; SpectrumType/@energyCalibrationReference; both Annex B examples

N4242-RESOLUTION.label: Energy-dependent spectral resolution calibration
N4242-RESOLUTION.definition: Keep the pairs of energy and peak full width at half maximum, any matched one-sigma width uncertainties, and any link from a spectrum to this calibration.
N4242-RESOLUTION.reason: A sensor resolution or generic uncertainty alone provides no peak-width curve with which to interpret a peak at a particular energy.
N4242-RESOLUTION.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, FWHMCalibrationType; SpectrumType/@FWHMCalibrationReference; Schematron EnergyFWHMMatch; Annex C

N4242-EFFICIENCY.label: Energy-dependent detector efficiency and its reference basis
N4242-EFFICIENCY.definition: Preserve ordered energy and efficiency pairs, their optional 1-sigma absolute uncertainties, and the calibration basis. Total and full-energy peak efficiencies use photons emitted; intrinsic full-energy and escape-peak efficiencies use photons incident on the detector. Preserve the applicable calibrated-peak references from spectra.
N4242-EFFICIENCY.reason: Numerically similar calibration factors can qualify different photons or peaks and different denominators. A generic calibration point does not preserve this basis.
N4242-EFFICIENCY.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, EfficiencyCalibrationType; TotalEfficiencyCalibration, FullEnergyPeakEfficiencyCalibration, IntrinsicFullEnergyPeakEfficiencyCalibration, IntrinsicSingleEscapePeakEfficiencyCalibration, IntrinsicDoubleEscapePeakEfficiencyCalibration; SpectrumType; Annexes C/E

N4242-WINDOWS.label: Gross counts for specified energy windows and counts since reset
N4242-WINDOWS.definition: Associate whole-range or window-specific counts with the detector and any window definition. Distinguish counts accumulated during this measurement from totals since reset. Preserve the pairing of ordered lower and upper window energies.
N4242-WINDOWS.reason: A standalone count or running total is ambiguous without the energy interval over which photons were counted and the time or reset basis.
N4242-WINDOWS.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, GrossCountsType/CountData, TotalCountData, @energyWindowsReference; EnergyWindowsType; Schematron WindowStartEndMatch, WindowStartEndCheck; Annex D

N4242-QC.label: Inspection time and reported calibration fitness for service
N4242-QC.definition: Record when the radiation instrument was inspected and whether that inspection reported it properly calibrated and fit for service.
N4242-QC.reason: An in-progress calibration, last calibration result or calibration date does not establish the dated fitness-for-service assessment.

N4242-LINEAGE.label: Measurement grouping and links from derived results to raw readings
N4242-LINEAGE.definition: Preserve measurement-group membership, references from derived values to their contributing raw spectra, gross counts, dose or exposure values of the same kind, and analysis links to measurements, groups or derived data. The raw-source reference is required for the corresponding value inside DerivedData and prohibited outside it, according to the XSD annotations.
N4242-LINEAGE.reason: A processing-stage label or copied-event relationship cannot identify exactly which raw readings produced the displayed derived result and which records entered analysis.
N4242-LINEAGE.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, RadMeasurementType/@radMeasurementGroupReferences, RadMeasurementGroupType, DerivedDataType, SpectrumType/@radRawSpectrumReferences, AnalysisResultsType source references; Annex E

N4242-ALGORITHM.label: Analysis execution, algorithm settings and reported status
N4242-ALGORITHM.definition: Associate an analysis with its start, computation duration, named algorithm and creator, versioned algorithm components, settings with values and units, and the reported analysis status or confidence where supplied.
N4242-ALGORITHM.reason: A reusable procedure or software revision alone cannot reproduce the configuration actually reported for a result or place its execution status and confidence in context.
N4242-ALGORITHM.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, AnalysisResultsType; AnalysisAlgorithmSettingType; AnalysisAlgorithmVersionType; Annex C

N4242-NUCLIDE.label: Nuclide identification, activity and detection limit
N4242-NUCLIDE.definition: Keep each named nuclide and its identification indicator distinct from confidence expressed as a description or percentage, any one-sigma uncertainty in that percentage, estimated activity at measurement time, one-sigma activity uncertainty, and that nuclide’s minimum detectable activity. Preserve any fit statistic at the analysis-result level.
N4242-NUCLIDE.reason: A radiation reading, reported isotope or confidence alone cannot tell the reader whether a nuclide was identified, its estimated activity versus detection limit, or the fit of the analysis as a whole.
N4242-NUCLIDE.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, NuclideType; NuclideIdentificationConfidence substitution group; NuclideAnalysisResultsType/NuclideAnalysisReducedChiSquareValue; Annex C

N4242-SOURCE.label: Estimated nuclide source geometry, shielding and position
N4242-SOURCE.definition: Associate the nuclide with assessed source geometry, estimated shielding effective atomic number and areal density, and a source position when reported. Preserve whether position is geographic, descriptive or relative to a stated origin.
N4242-SOURCE.reason: A detector coordinate, target bearing or generic event shape does not identify the source-specific geometry and shielding estimates used to explain a radiation result.
N4242-SOURCE.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, NuclideType/NuclideSourceGeometryCode, NuclideShieldingAtomicNumber, NuclideShieldingArealDensityValue, SourcePosition; SourcePositionType; RelativeLocationType

N4242-PEAK.label: Spectral peak energy, width and continuum-subtracted area
N4242-PEAK.definition: Report measured peak energy and, when supplied, expected peak energy, full width at half maximum, continuum-subtracted net counts, and absolute 1-sigma uncertainty of the net counts. Preserve the source recommendation against further adjustments such as environmental-background subtraction.
N4242-PEAK.reason: A recorded maximum or signal frequency is insufficient to distinguish a fitted peak’s location, width and net count from the underlying spectrum and calibration curve.
N4242-PEAK.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, SpectrumPeakAnalysisResultsType/SpectrumPeak; SpectrumPeakType; Annex C

N4242-RATES.label: Dose, exposure and count rates with distinct accumulation bases
N4242-RATES.definition: Distinguish ambient dose equivalent, exposure and event counts, their rate versus accumulated forms, and detector measurements since reset versus analysis totals over selected inputs. Retain background and summary statistics with the quantity they qualify.
N4242-RATES.reason: The prior radiation reading includes absorbed dose. Absorbed dose, ambient dose equivalent and exposure have different physical meanings; the same-looking total can also span a different interval.
N4242-RATES.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, DoseRateType, ExposureRateType, TotalDose, TotalExposure, DoseAnalysisResultsType, ExposureAnalysisResultsType, GrossCountAnalysisResultsType; Annex D

N4242-ALARM.label: Radiation alarm detector attribution, energy windows and annunciation
N4242-ALARM.definition: Identify the alarm category, contributing detector references and any energy-window indices that triggered the alarm. Keep audible indication and light color alongside the reported alarm.
N4242-ALARM.reason: A general alert lifecycle cannot explain which detector and energy range triggered a radiation alarm or how the instrument signalled it.
N4242-ALARM.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, RadAlarmType/@radDetectorInformationReferences, RadAlarmEnergyWindowIndices, AlarmAudibleIndicator, RadAlarmLightColor; Annex D alarm example

N4242-CHAR.label: Individual characteristic and group out-of-limits indications
N4242-CHAR.definition: Associate each supplemental characteristic with its name, reported value and any recorded sampling time or limit indication. Keep its units and declared data class with that value. A group can exceed a high or low control limit because of one member or a combination of members. Preserve the separately reported group indication.
N4242-CHAR.reason: A grouped value or threshold does not say whether an exception applies to one characteristic or to the group and which item, instrument or detector it describes.
N4242-CHAR.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, CharacteristicType/@valueDateTime, @valueOutOfLimits; CharacteristicGroupType/@groupOutOfLimits; RadDetectorCharacteristics, RadItemCharacteristics, RadInstrumentCharacteristics; Annex L

N4242-MEDIA.label: Acquisition context linking measured items and multimedia
N4242-MEDIA.definition: When supplied, retain the measured-item reference and the media capture device, view, capture time and duration, content location or encoding. Record sequenceNumber as the increasing processing order of multiple multimedia records, independently of when they were captured.
N4242-MEDIA.reason: A media attachment to an observation or a selected frame cannot by itself identify the recorded item, capture device, view and acquisition interval of the supporting evidence.
N4242-MEDIA.locator: NIST 2020 edition XSD, MultimediaDataType/@radItemInformationReferences, @sequenceNumber, MultimediaDeviceIdentifier, ImagePerspectiveCode, MultimediaCaptureStartDateTime and MultimediaCaptureDuration

N4242-ELEVATION-REFERENCE.label: Ellipsoid elevation, surface offset and their separate accuracy estimates
N4242-ELEVATION-REFERENCE.definition: Keep elevation relative to the applicable ellipsoid separate from the vertical difference to the earth’s surface. Associate horizontal position, elevation and elevation-offset accuracy with their respective quantities. The N42 horizontal accuracy is one sigma; the two vertical accuracy annotations do not specify that convention.
N4242-ELEVATION-REFERENCE.reason: A geographic position or generic error field cannot identify the reference surface of each vertical distance or which uncertainty qualifies which value.

N4242-FAULT-OUTPUT.label: Reported fault impact on operation and trust in its output
N4242-FAULT-OUTPUT.definition: Associate the fault with an instrument, detector or analysis. Report separately whether operation terminated, was seriously disrupted or continued with at most minor disruption, and whether the resulting data are untrustworthy or potentially untrustworthy under the reported severity.
N4242-FAULT-OUTPUT.reason: A health indicator, individual alert severity or generic confidence does not state whether the associated operation still produced output suitable for use.

summary_cells.A1: Current comparison · RFC 8348 and N42.42 corrective review · 22 November 2026
summary_cells.B1: 608 information rows, 23 columns and 26 worksheets. Columns P and Q contain the revised comparisons. 7 new candidates appear in rows 639–645. Both revised assessments await owner disposition.

method: Partitioned all 601 prior decisions by relation, subject, classification, repeated explanations and evidence standing. Examined direct and partial decisions against their actual target definition, relation-only near misses, the nine case holds, and negative families for source-native exceptions. Recorded material decisions with exact locators.

Parsed the intake-pinned schema, Schematron and eleven originals; compared equipment versus analysis vs record roles, optional attributes, conditional validation, example-defined characteristics, and the meaning of shared units. Focused on portable donor concepts versus implementation-specific values.

Retained grouped negative decisions when the family shares an actual scope boundary (e.g., camera control requests and delivery protocols). Split ambiguity where the same rationale concealed different subjects or reference quantities. Kept the nine case holds separate from schema-level evidence.
Checked the 19 donor-native candidate rows against the native reread and incorporated the revised definitions in donor cells.

before.reason: A result in the instrument file can identify its contributing detector. External member visibility, capability exposure and interface mediation remain separate.

after.reason: A measurement can refer to the detector that collected it. Document-level attribution supplies no capability-publication or member-visibility policy for a composition interface.

before.reason: Spectral channels are bins within detector output. The detector reference identifies its source, without creating a separately addressable transducer channel.

after.reason: In this spectrum an energy channel is a bin in a sequence of counts. The spectrum can point to detector information; the bin has no independent transducer address.

before.reason: The file describes the collecting instrument. A spectrum also references the particular detector used. A publisher or file creator has a different role.

after.reason: Instrument information identifies the collecting instrument. The XSD allows the detector reference on a spectrum to be omitted; the Schematron separately checks same-detector spectrum siblings within a measurement. Creator identity applies to the file.

before.reason: An analysis can report the identity of a nuclide and confidence in its identification. This is a domain-specific classification; target behavior is a different assertion.

after.reason: Nuclide name, identification status and algorithm-dependent certainty refer to a radiation analysis. They do not classify the behavior or target hypothesis of a SAPIENT detection.

before.reason: An item or source may have angles relative to an origin. The observer and orientation basis used by the target row require explicit corroboration.

after.reason: RelativeLocationAzimuthValue provides a bearing from a reference point. Confirm that the Origin identifies the observer and check its directional convention before comparing the ISA bearing.

before.reason: The measured item may have scalar speed and orientation. Its facing orientation is insufficient to establish the direction of the velocity vector.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadItemStateType/StateVector; SpeedValue documentation, OrientationType
after.reason: SpeedValue is scalar. Its definition explicitly assigns direction along the orientation bearing when Orientation is present. Without that bearing the item speed alone gives no velocity direction.

before.locator: NIST add-in XSD, HumidityValue and TemperatureValue substitutions for RadMeasurementExtension; primary XSD extension elements
before.reason: An author may define an extension in a separate namespace via an XML schema. This is schema-level extensibility; an individual device need not transmit a custom-type declaration.

after.locator: NIST add-in XSD, HumidityValue and TemperatureValue substitutions for RadMeasurementExtension; primary XSD extension elements
after.reason: An external schema can declare elements substituting for an extension point. The NIST add-in declares two simple elements; it does not demonstrate a component reporting a named custom structure and its field catalogue.

before.locator: NIST add-in XSD, HumidityValue and TemperatureValue; primary XSD RadMeasurementType/RadMeasurementExtension
before.reason: A schema extension gives its field a name, type, role and documentation. These field definitions reside in the schema rather than being declared by the reporting component.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadMeasurementExtension substitution group; illustrative N42SchemaAddin-2020.xsd/HumidityValue, TemperatureValue
after.reason: An externally declared extension element has a name and a type. These schema-level field definitions provide part of a custom field contract. Instance-specific capability declarations and omission rules for a device-defined structure are separate.

before.reason: Schema occurrence constraints describe repeatable results and list-valued channel data. A device does not declare runtime tree-depth or collection limits in this record.

after.reason: The XSD constrains repetitions of document elements and declares a list type for channel data. These rules govern documents; an equipment declaration of the permitted shape and bounds for its own property has no established counterpart.

before.locator: N42 2020 XSD, Angle90Type, Angle180Type and associated simple types
before.reason: The schema constrains some angular values and uses enumerations for coded fields. It does not describe a component publishing its own range or exclusions.

after.locator: N42 2020 XSD, Angle90Type, Angle180Type and associated simple types
after.reason: N42 defines restricted types and code lists in its publication. An instance reporting a characteristic does not thereby publish the device-specific allowed and excluded values of that property.

before.reason: Producers of the document or its analysis algorithm can be named. The format does not require the full issuer, edition, evidence locator and standing of each assertion.

after.reason: The file may name its producing organization and separately the creator of an analysis algorithm. Those names apply to defined subjects. A source/issuer and evidence locator for each individual assertion are not provided.

before.reason: Explicit references link processed values or analyses to source data. A document link alone does not prove that two separate digital copies correspond to one original physical event.

after.reason: Within-document references associate calculated values with their raw inputs. They do not distinguish an original physical event from multiple digital copies of its record, which is the identity issue on this row.

before.reason: An analysis can identify contributing measurements, groups and derived products. A network fusion node and its time-qualified detection identities require additional evidence.

after.reason: Source measurements for an analysis can be referenced. Neither this reference nor group membership identifies a contributing detection in a network-fused detection.

before.reason: Internal references establish data provenance from a result back to source measurements; they do not identify an earlier network message by sender, time or conversation.

after.reason: An analysis can refer to one or more source measurements by XML ID. This is record-level derivation within the document; no source-message address, original sender or conversation identifier is asserted.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD RadInstrumentVersionType; NIST Annex C, RadInstrumentVersion[RadInstrumentComponentName=Hardware]
before.reason: An instrument identifies a named component and its version. The edition example explicitly identifies Hardware and its version.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadInstrumentVersion, RadInstrumentVersionType; hardware-labelled examples in Annexes C and D
after.reason: RadInstrumentVersion pairs a component name with a version. Published examples label a component Hardware. Its scope follows the named component; the XSD has no dedicated requirement for a whole-instrument hardware revision.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD RadInstrumentVersionType; NIST Annex B, RadInstrumentVersion[RadInstrumentComponentName=Software]
before.reason: The instrument reports the version for its named software component. Analysis algorithm versions have a separate subject.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadInstrumentVersion documentation and RadInstrumentVersionType; Annex B
after.reason: The RadInstrumentVersion annotation calls for Software to identify software and/or firmware that produced the current document. That identifies the producer version; it does not inventory every program executing on a component.

before.reason: The standard gives explicit true-north, horizontal-plane and body-axis references. Their equivalence to a source field with unresolved frame semantics remains open.

after.reason: OrientationType defines body axes, the local horizontal plane and true north. ISA-Q003 leaves the compared orientation frame open; directional equivalence cannot be assigned until that question is settled.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex C Bias and Annex G HV
before.reason: Example detector characteristics carry a bias or high voltage in volts. They do not establish DC load-side versus source-side voltage.

after.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex C Bias and Annex G HV
after.reason: Detector Bias and HV are illustrative voltage characteristics. Neither the example name nor the unit V identifies DC voltage at the electrical load terminals.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex C Bias and Annex G HV
before.reason: Example detector characteristics carry a bias or high voltage in volts. They do not establish DC load-side versus source-side voltage.

after.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex C Bias and Annex G HV
after.reason: The example HV and Bias values are attached to detector characteristics. No source-side power-supply terminal or AC/DC convention is identified.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex F and Annex I, RadioSignalStrength
before.reason: Illustrative instrument-state values give radio signal strength in dBm. Their reference point, link endpoint and name are not standardized as a receive-power field.

after.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex F and Annex I, RadioSignalStrength
after.reason: Annex F and I illustrate a named RadioSignalStrength value in dBm. Neither receiving endpoint nor link direction is identified; an absolute power unit alone cannot establish receiver input power.

before.reason: Analysis completion and confidence qualify an analysis result. They do not provide an equipment-wide output-quality setting.

after.reason: The fault severity class qualifies trust in data produced by an affected operation. Fatal and Error designate untrustworthy data; Warning allows uncertainty. This provides conditional output-quality evidence without a general imaging-quality grade.

before.reason: A fault carries a code, explanation and severity. Neither an equipment tamper flag nor cryptographic-key-filled state is designated.

after.reason: FaultCodeValue and FaultDescription can describe problems for an instrument during acquisition. The dedicated fields and examples examined do not establish a detector-tamper indicator.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex F/I BatteryCharge and RadioSignalStrength
before.reason: Example percent charge and absolute dBm measurements have specific subjects. They cannot resolve the reference quantity for “Level value — meaning question”; the ISA interpretation question stands.

after.locator: ISA-Q001; NIST illustrative Annex F BatteryCharge; core CharacteristicType
after.reason: ISA-Q001 holds the subject and reference of Level in percent. Annex F shows an instrument-specific percentage charge, with an explicit battery subject; that cannot identify the subject of the ISA field.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex F/I BatteryCharge and RadioSignalStrength
before.reason: Example percent charge and absolute dBm measurements have specific subjects. They cannot resolve the reference quantity for “Link Loss value — reference question”; the ISA interpretation question stands.

after.locator: ISA-Q002; NIST illustrative Annex F RadioSignalStrength; core CharacteristicType
after.reason: ISA-Q002 leaves the link-loss basis unresolved. Annex F reports a single radio strength in dBm. It lacks the two endpoint values or gain/loss convention needed to compare a link-loss value in dB.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD CharacteristicType; NIST Annex F/I BatteryCharge and RadioSignalStrength
before.reason: Example percent charge and absolute dBm measurements have specific subjects. They cannot resolve the reference quantity for “Signal Strength Ratio — reference quantity question”; the ISA interpretation question stands.

after.locator: ISA-Q004; NIST illustrative Annex I RadioSignalStrength; core CharacteristicType
after.reason: ISA-Q004 leaves the reference quantity of the signal-strength ratio unresolved. An example absolute strength in dBm does not identify the two quantities forming that ratio.

before.reason: An alarm can identify the contributing detectors and belong to an analysis result. An event message sender and a general messaging scope are separate roles.

after.reason: Detector references identify equipment associated with a radiation alarm within an analysis. Neither a modeled message-event source nor an independent observable scope is declared by these references.

before.reason: A document can have its own ID and contain several linked records and groups. A file-server package identity, lifecycle and membership contract need separate evidence.

after.reason: A document UUID identifies this particular XML document. Internal references connect its data objects; they do not provide a managed package identity or declared package-to-record associations.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD FaultType; RadInstrumentStateType/Fault, RadDetectorStateType/Fault, AnalysisResultsType/Fault
before.reason: Equipment and analysis can each report coded faults and severity. A separate overall health assessment or aggregation rule does not follow from fault records alone.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD FaultType, FaultSeverityCodeSimpleType, RadDetectorStateType, RadInstrumentStateType, AnalysisResultsType
after.reason: Instrument or detector state can report a fault, code and severity, and an analysis can report its own fault. Severity distinguishes termination, serious disruption and a warning, including their consequences for trust in the data. No hierarchy-wide health calculation is specified.

before.reason: Faults can be attached to the equipment state for a dated measurement. Log retention, deletion or historical retrieval are outside this exchange.

after.reason: A dated measurement can carry an equipment fault. A collection of such files does not by itself constitute the managed log, retention or deletion capability in the row.

before.locator: 2020 NIST XSD AnalysisAlgorithmSettingType, RadInstrumentCharacteristics; NIST Annex E AnalysisAlgorithmSetting
before.reason: A result can document algorithm parameters and values used. Their presence does not imply user control, an equipment-wide configuration or security settings.

after.locator: 2020 NIST XSD AnalysisAlgorithmSettingType, RadInstrumentCharacteristics; NIST Annex E AnalysisAlgorithmSetting
after.reason: AnalysisAlgorithmSetting records a setting used by the analysis. It does not establish that the value is a user-modifiable configuration of the equipment or a security setting.

before.reason: A spectrum links channel counts to detector and calibration metadata. Physical waveform streaming, independent metadata connections and their transport timing are different subjects.

after.reason: Calibration and detector references accompany an exchanged spectrum. The record does not declare a separately transported metadata stream or its alignment with an independently timed digital waveform.

before.reason: Search and long-dwell modes distinguish acquisition behavior in a reported measurement. Mode persistence, tracking capability and operator tasking are separate declarations.

after.reason: A reported Search or Long Dwell mode distinguishes what the instrument was doing at acquisition. It does not declare how long a mode persists, whether its field of view can be steered, or what tracking behavior is supported.

before.reason: A manufacturer can identify the model using a name or model number. The number is not explicitly an orderable catalog code.

after.reason: RadInstrumentModelName can hold a manufacturer model name, number or description. A value in that field cannot be treated as an orderable commercial product code without manufacturer evidence.

before.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · RadInstrumentVersionType / RadInstrumentComponentName, RadInstrumentComponentVersion; RadInstrumentManufacturerName
before.reason: The instrument record identifies the manufacturer and names individual components with versions. A distinct whole-device revision, build lot or engineering-change level requires additional evidence.

after.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · RadInstrumentVersionType / RadInstrumentComponentName, RadInstrumentComponentVersion; RadInstrumentManufacturerName
after.reason: The published version pair identifies a named instrument component and its version. No defined aggregate device revision can be inferred by combining hardware and software examples.

before.reason: Calibration arrays associate energy points with efficiency or resolution values. These fitted or calibrated values do not by themselves identify applied inputs and actual observed readouts.

after.reason: The calibration curves associate energies with efficiency or peak width. Those arrays can supply paired calibration values. They do not identify a physical test stimulus and measured as-found readout at each calibration step.

before.reason: A reduced chi-square quantifies agreement between observed and predicted nuclide-analysis data. The other technique-specific noise and readout diagnostics require separate evidence.

after.reason: The reduced chi-square qualifies agreement between predicted and observed values in nuclide analysis. The compared PA-DIM techniques report signal-fit and noise diagnostics with different statistics; the chi-square is not their correlation coefficient or noise ratio.

before.reason: The instrument, measurement and analysis blocks define radiation exchange records. Their declared fields do not establish Chromatogram features and sample injection context.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD SpectrumPeakType, SpectrumPeakFWHMValue, SpectrumPeakNetAreaValue; PA-DIM row definition
after.reason: Both analyses can characterize a peak by width and area. N42 reports a peak on an energy axis and defines net counts after continuum subtraction. A chromatogram uses a retention-time axis and sample-injection context.

before.reason: Instrument classes distinguish purposes such as dosimetry, radionuclide identification and portal monitoring. The format does not separately formalize an arbitrary user goal.

after.reason: An instrument class such as Dosimeter or Portal Monitor suggests intended use. It does not declare a user goal separately from a device class or a performed measurement.

before.reason: A measurement can include instrument state with Test mode. The field describes the instrument during collection and does not independently identify an external controller or mode at later record creation.

after.reason: Test is a defined radiation-instrument operating mode during collection. It can establish the instrument was testing. It supplies no independent controller state or proof that record creation occurred at the same time.

before.reason: A spectrum references the detector information in this document. A sensor-selective capture command and support declaration are separate.

after.reason: The XML Schema makes the spectrum detector ID reference optional, and Schematron tests detector reference target and sibling cardinality in a measurement. A referenced detector is document-scoped. The exchange does not advertise selective capture.

before.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · RadInstrumentVersionType / RadInstrumentComponentName, RadInstrumentComponentVersion; RadInstrumentManufacturerName
before.reason: The instrument record identifies the manufacturer and names individual components with versions. A distinct whole-device revision, build lot or engineering-change level requires additional evidence.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD RadInstrumentManufacturerName, RadDetectorCharacteristics; Annex C detector CharacteristicName=Vendor
after.reason: RadInstrumentManufacturerName names the instrument manufacturer. Annex C shows a detector characteristic named Vendor. Neither establishes separate assembly producer/vendor roles with build time and engineering change level.

before.reason: A spectrum identifies its detector, derived spectra can reference raw spectra, and a measurement can identify measured items. The fields establish document links, distinct from a service excerpt URI.

after.reason: The item link from a measurement identifies what is measured. A spectrum may carry detector identity and can reference raw spectra in a derived product. These document references distinguish roles but are not a service excerpt URI.

before.reason: Average rates are calculated over the input measurements, which carry acquisition durations. No independent flag indicates that samples fill a configured averaging interval.

after.reason: AverageCountRateValue summarizes all measurements chosen for analysis. Input elapsed duration provides acquisition context, not configured sample spacing, target averaging duration or achieved coverage.

before.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · GrossCountsType/CountData, LiveTimeDuration; RadMeasurementType/StartDateTime; TotalDose
before.reason: Counts belong to a timed measurement; total dose accumulates since the last instrument reset. An explicit reset instant is not carried by the total-dose value.

after.locator: NIST 2020 XSD GrossCountsType, CountData, TotalCountData, TotalDose, TotalExposure; RadMeasurementType/StartDateTime
after.reason: Acquisition counts can be timed using measurement start and detector live duration. TotalCountData, TotalDose and TotalExposure instead accumulate since instrument reset. A reset timestamp is not required on those values.

before.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · CharacteristicType; illustrative Annex H, I and L instrument characteristics/BatteryCharge
before.reason: Named instrument characteristics in the examples report a percentage of battery charge. The vocabulary and capacity basis are example-specific. Rated capacity, battery health and discharge cycles need additional evidence.

after.locator: NIST illustrative Annexes F and I BatteryCharge; core CharacteristicType
after.reason: The BatteryCharge example is a percentage. It does not give rated capacity and the declining maximum capacity separately, or identify an energy or charge denominator.

before.locator: NIST 2020 n42.xsd · CharacteristicType; illustrative Annex H, I and L instrument characteristics/BatteryCharge
